### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s).

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx`  _(via formatRange (literal, a string literal in SHIM; a string literal in installSandboxIntl), formatRangeToParts (literal, a string literal in SHIM; a string literal in installSandboxIntl), formatToParts (literal, a string literal in SHIM; a string literal in installSandboxIntl), resolvedOptions (literal, a string literal in SHIM; a string literal in installSandboxIntl), timeZone (literal, a string literal in DATE_TIME_FORMAT_OPTION_KEYS))_
- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via JobSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via JobSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via timeZone (literal, a string literal in DATE_TIME_FORMAT_OPTION_KEYS))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-7.mdx`  _(via JobSchema (symbol, a top-level const))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e1ae1315c60cf8a21a5290646779d632dddc0e2b` — the merge of head `aed5e2959f15158dac89cb24d1f280486b42e628` into base `ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e1ae1315c60cf8a21a5290646779d632dddc0e2b && git checkout e1ae1315c60cf8a21a5290646779d632dddc0e2b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f aed5e2959f15158dac89cb24d1f280486b42e628 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f && git merge --no-ff aed5e2959f15158dac89cb24d1f280486b42e628

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab085a048241b0bf1fde06696fc6cbf659a6707f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aed5e2959f15158dac89cb24d1f280486b42e628`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts + content/docs/references/system/job.mdx (regenerated from it), content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx (the sandbox claim the text makes), packages/runtime/src/sandbox/sandbox-intl.ts and packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts (the capability the text asserts), packages/cli/src/utils/detect-free-identifiers.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/extract-hook-body.ts and packages/cli/src/utils/sandbox-globals-probe.test.ts (the lowering claim), .changeset/28898-sandbox-intl-date-time-format.md

Reviewed: the net diff of `aed5e295` against merge-base `a3640933` (3 commits, 14 files, +860/−33), card #28898 with triage `6568654195`, the claim `6569189598` and the os-dev-report `6570529017`, the PR body, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the PR was read from the fetched objects, no worktree.

### ① Derived judgments

**Schema face (the `hits` path).** `packages/spec/src/system/job.zod.ts` changes one `.describe()` string and its docblock on `JobSchema.handler`; the Zod chain (`z.string().optional()`) is byte-identical. Accept set unchanged: right. `content/docs/references/system/job.mdx` carries the same sentence (one row, the `handler` cell); no other committed artifact held the old text, so the regeneration is complete: right. The sentence asserts a runtime fact ("`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with a `timeZone` option is available in the sandbox (nothing else of `Intl` is)"); read against `sandbox-intl.ts` it is true on this head (one own member, `DateTimeFormat`, `Intl` non-enumerable, the constructor whole). Prime Directive 10's corollary (never advertise what the runtime does not deliver) holds.

**Sandbox safety — the main question.** Read `sandbox-intl.ts` and the `execute()` seam in `quickjs-runner.ts` line by line.

- *What crosses, in.* The VM-side shim calls `host(op, stringify({ l, o }), a, b)`: `op` is a shim-chosen literal, the JSON string is produced by `JSON.stringify` captured at install, `a`/`b` pass through `Number()` (or `undefined`, which the shim replaces with the VM's own `Date.now()` for `format`/`formatToParts` and leaves `undefined` for the range calls, so the host sees exactly what it would see natively). The host reads them with `vm.getString` and `vm.dump` on number handles; nothing is retained. `readSnapshot` re-parses the JSON on the host and copies only the twenty ECMA-402 option keys with primitive values into a fresh object, and accepts locales only as a primitive or an array of primitives. No body-chosen key is ever assigned on the host (`__proto__` in the JSON cannot land anywhere), and no VM object is handed to the host `Intl`. Right.
- *What crosses, out.* One `vm.newString(JSON.stringify(answer))`; `answer` is `{ ok, value }` or `{ ok: false, name, message }`. `value` is a string, a parts array, a resolved-options object or a locale list — all JSON-plain. The VM parses it with the captured `JSON.parse`, so every object a body receives is VM-made (pinned by the isolation test: `Object.prototype` / `Array.prototype`, fresh per call). No host object, function, prototype or error object reaches the VM: verified.
- *The bridge.* `host` is passed as the one argument of the shim factory and the host-side handle is disposed after install; the VM function survives only inside the shim's closure. No global names it (pinned: the only `/intl|bridge/i` global is `Intl`). A body cannot reach it through `caller`/`arguments.callee` (strict shim). Verified.
- *Host errors.* Everything in the callback, `vm.getString` included, is inside one `try`; the catch forwards only `name` (whitelisted to `RangeError`/`TypeError`, else `Error`) and `message` as strings. The VM constructs its own `RangeError`/`TypeError`/`Error` from the message, so the stack a body sees is the VM's. No host stack, path or object leaks. The messages are the host's own ICU sentences (e.g. the invalid-zone text), which is what the order asked for. Right.
- *Unbounded host work.* A sync host callback runs inside the VM slice, so its time is charged to the body's CPU budget by the next interrupt check (`cpuMs + (now − sliceStart)`), and the wall ceiling backs it. Input size is bounded by the VM memory cap (32 MB default): a huge locale string or option value reaches the host once, costs O(n) and is refused by ICU with a `RangeError` before it is cached; a long but valid locale array costs the host O(n) canonicalisation per call, bounded by the same budget. `formatRange` is two numbers in, one string out. The per-invocation formatter cache is keyed by the raw snapshot and capped at 64 entries, cleared wholesale and dropped with the VM; its worst case is 64 × (a snapshot that fits the VM heap), reachable only by a body that spends its own CPU budget building distinct multi-megabyte valid snapshots. Bounded by the existing limits; no new amplification class. Right, with one note under ③.
- *Clock and I/O.* "Now" is the VM's `Date.now` captured at install (pinned: a body replacing `Date.now` or `JSON.stringify` steers nothing). Formatting performs no I/O. Right.
- *The L1 path.* `installSandboxIntl` runs before the expression branch, so L1 expressions get it too; the host call is synchronous, so a sync expression can use it. Consistent with "every body kind".
- *`supportedLocalesOf` and `resolvedOptions`.* Both answer values only. A default-constructed formatter's `resolvedOptions()` reports the host's default locale and time zone (the dev's own flag). Judged acceptable, and the default should NOT be pinned in this PR — see ③ for the recommendation and its reasons.

No sandbox-escape-class finding. No private record was written.

**One seam.** `QuickJSScriptRunner.execute()` is the only place a VM is made; every production `new QuickJSScriptRunner` (five sites: `app-plugin.ts` ×2, `app-artifact-handlers.ts` ×3) is wrapped by `hookBodyRunnerFactory`, `actionBodyRunnerFactory` or `jobBodyRunnerFactory`; the only other `ScriptRunner` implementor is `UnimplementedScriptRunner`, which throws. So hook, action and job bodies (and L1 expressions) share the global set — the order's conditional ("if they share it, they get the same, and say so in the changeset") is met, and the changeset, the PR body and `jobs.mdx` each say so in words. Honest and intended. Right.

**CLI lowering (`detect-free-identifiers.ts`, `extract-hook-body.ts`).** Needed: `sandbox-globals-probe.test.ts` measures the real sandbox against the two sets, so with `Intl` now present the base's `NODE_ONLY_GLOBALS` entry `Intl` would red the partition pin, and moving `Intl` wholesale into `SANDBOX_GLOBALS` would lower a handler using `Intl.NumberFormat` into a body that throws (`TypeError` now, not `ReferenceError`) — the #14301 class. Judging per member (`MEMBER_JUDGED_GLOBALS = {Intl}`; a non-computed `Intl.NAME` read is recorded as `Intl.NAME`; a bare or computed use stays reported as `Intl`, the bundling direction; a local named `Intl` binds its members through the root) is the smallest correct change, and the probe test now measures the namespace present and every dotted member under a listed namespace. Right.
Behaviour of an existing handler after lowering: a handler that used only `Intl.DateTimeFormat` was bundled on the base and will lower on its next `os build`; because the sandbox answers with the host's own `Intl.DateTimeFormat`, its output, its default locale and zone, and its errors are the in-process ones. The one divergence I can construct is a BigInt or Symbol passed as `locales` (the shim passes `undefined` where the host throws `TypeError`), which no real handler does. `Date.prototype.toLocale*` with a `timeZone` option is a method, not a free identifier, so such a handler lowered before this PR as well; the dev's out-of-scope note on it is accurate and not introduced here. Right.
Published cli `hook-body` subpath: `HookBodyExtractionError`'s members, types and readonly-ness are unchanged (`published-subpath-hook-body.pin.test.ts` asserts exactly `kind`, `originLabel`, `freeIdentifiers`, `nodeOnlyIdentifiers`); only the values can now be a dotted spelling (`Intl.NumberFormat`). The module-scope refusal sentence that the docs quote is byte-identical; the host-only branch gained a parenthesis and dropped the word `ReferenceError`, and nothing in `content/docs` or the tests quotes that branch. Right.

**Metadata and migration text.** `jobs.mdx` gains one bullet; the example passes `timeZone`; the feature test it names is the one the order asked for. Right.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `@objectstack/cli` patch, `@objectstack/spec` patch, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and in the changeset body. Matches.
- `Clause-②: no` is right: no exported name, type, schema shape or error code moves. The sandbox's globals are not a published accept set — `ScriptBodySchema.source` is `z.string()` and no spec schema declares what it may call — so a body gaining a global is runtime capability, as the order expected. The cli subpath value change (a diagnostic string array that can now carry `Intl.NAME`) is a value, not a member or a type; the shape pin is green, and the changeset names the change in words. Not a widening of a published surface.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value, type or default moves; `handler` stays accepted and deprecated; the text change ships as description. `none` takes patch; spec patch is the floor for shipped description text.
- No BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 disposition owed.

### ③ Boundary flags

- *Dev flag 1 (open_questions is empty; carried in out_of_scope_findings): a default-constructed formatter's `resolvedOptions()` tells a body the server's default locale and time zone.* Answered: acceptable as values; recommend NOT pinning the default to UTC or en-US. Reasons: (a) the order's contract is "behaves as the host's for the same input", and the cli now lowers a handler on the strength of that equivalence — a pinned default would make a lowered handler answer differently from its in-process original; (b) the sandbox's own `Date` already runs in the host's local zone (QuickJS resolves the offset through the host, which is why `toLocaleString` formats in the server zone, as the dev observed), so a pinned `Intl` default would give a body two different "default zones"; (c) the zone was already derivable from `new Date().getTimezoneOffset()`, and the default locale is deployment configuration, not a secret. Determinism across hosts is the author's to declare by passing `timeZone` (and a locale), which every example in this PR does. Follow-up, not blocking: one sentence in `jobs.mdx` saying the default locale and zone are the server's, so always pass `timeZone`.
- *Dev flag 2: `Date.prototype.toLocaleString(locale, { timeZone })` ignores its arguments in QuickJS.* Pre-existing, outside this diff, no measured reach; noting it is the right disposition under Prime Directive 10 (a note, since there is no reproduced defect at a public door yet). Not escalated.
- *Cache memory note (mine, not blocking):* the formatter cache is keyed by the raw snapshot string; a hostile body can hold up to 64 distinct valid snapshots on the host for the life of one invocation, each bounded by the VM heap and paid for in its own CPU budget. Existing limits bound it; a smaller key or cap would only tighten a bound that already exists.
- *Evidence read, not re-run (read-only shape).* Red on base: all 12 new runtime cases evaluate `Intl` inside the VM, so 12/12 `ReferenceError: 'Intl' is not defined` on `a3640933` is the only possible reading, consistent with the report. Ablations: the runtime ablation count (12 red of 341) matches the file; the cli ablation's four names (the three lower-it pins plus the named-cases pin) are exactly the tests that assert `Intl.DateTimeFormat` lowers or is in `SANDBOX_GLOBALS`, and the dev's explanation of why the partition pin stays green is correct (a name in neither set is not probed, which is why the named-cases pin exists); the dogfood red leg on a rebuilt dist is described with its preflight markers both ways. Derived gates: `28898-gates-ran.txt` holds 108 lines, 108 at exit 0, and the report's `--ran` line reads 108/108 with 0 NOT-MEASURED. Consistent.
- *CI on the head at review time:* 24 success, 12 skipped, 31 in_progress (Test Core 1–8, Type Check lanes, Build Core, Test UI, Live E2E UI), 0 failed. `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` are success. The seat reads the check-runs again before enqueue; the landing's check-② is not this record's to grant.
- *Overlap:* 0 of the 44 open PRs touch `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/**`, the cli lowering files, `system/job.zod.ts`, `automation/jobs.mdx`, `references/system/job.mdx` or the dogfood file. None.
- *Author:* PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no author note owed.
- *Governed surfaces:* none touched (no `.claude/**`, `docs/adr/**`, workflows, `AGENTS.md`).

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-n1omdg`
Reviewed-by: `session_0186vfjHHMsRXC9EUT9hTFMo`

**VERDICT: PASS**
